notes: The requested buffering-capacity value is unavailable from the six pod metrics. Positive explanatory evidence is supplied per turn: alkalinity/ANC require acidimetric sample titration, and conductivity used for procedural choices is not a conversion to capacity. RAG is expected to support these explanations beyond the probe-only slice. Corpus absence conclusions are bounded to supplied sources; no live readings are promised.

turns.content: Before we call a pH drop at the mill creek a real event, I want to know how much acid that creek can soak up before the pH actually moves. Can our pods tell me that?

must_contain: States that the water's capacity to absorb acid is not one of the parameters this system measures
States plainly that the question cannot be answered from what the system measures
Notes that the corpus does contain a USGS chapter covering alkalinity and acid neutralizing capacity
Contrasts the sensor reading with a manual acid titration of a collected sample, which is the method the corpus does describe
States that the chapter gives no way to infer that capacity from any sensor-measurable parameter
Offers to describe the measured pH record if supplied, without inventing access or treating pH as a substitute for buffering capacity
must_not: answers using the alkalinity titration procedure as though it applied to a measured metric
reports an alkalinity or acid-neutralizing-capacity value, range, or typical figure as if the system could produce one
presents the alkalinity chapter's titration-curve pH landmarks such as 8.3, 4.5 or 5.5 as thresholds for the measured pH reading
invents a relationship converting a measured parameter into buffering capacity
silently substitutes the pH reading for the thing that was asked about

retrieval_evidence.quote: the acidimetric titration of a sample; the only difference is that the alkalinity sample is filtered,
Calculation of alkalinity or ANC is a simple accounting of the amount of acid used to neutralize
Vs 	is 	the volume of sample, in milliliters.

turns.content: Those pods are already logging pH and conductivity every fifteen minutes. Is there really no way to work it out from those two?

must_contain: States that no source in the corpus gives a relationship between the water's acid-absorbing capacity and specific conductance
States that no source gives a way to estimate one from the other
Distinguishes conductivity used for titration-method selection and recordkeeping from the acid-volume, acid-concentration and sample-volume inputs used to calculate alkalinity
States that the measured pH alone does not yield it either
Declines to produce an estimate rather than offering an approximate conversion
must_not: supplies a formula, ratio, or rule of thumb converting conductivity or pH into buffering capacity
treats the conductivity thresholds in the alkalinity chapter as an alkalinity-conductivity relationship
cites an external calculator or model as though its contents were available in the corpus
offers a hedged numeric estimate in place of a refusal
cites the specific-conductance chapter's statement that conductivity has been used to estimate major solute concentrations as a route to buffering capacity
